entries.note: A hooks module registers an event at most once without a matcher (validate and the loader refuse a second): mod/deliver.ts owns session.start, the join and classic.SessionStart (hello, the restore, the tail child), mod/prompt.ts owns prompt.submit (the gate, rows context, presence), mod/rows.ts owns classic.SubagentStop.

Modules are off only diskless or in a tool server's daemon (then by policy, safe mode, --bare): they load in -p and in a --bg worker such as the room's Claude. A --bg dispatch prompt reaches prompt.submit as origin composer (S2).

A classic.<Event> chain is [managed settings hooks, ...modules in load order, core], and core runs every other settings hook. A module that answers without next() therefore skips every non-managed settings hook for that call (its own plugin's, other plugins' and the user's and project's command hooks) and the modules of plugins loaded after it; managed hooks and earlier-loaded modules still run (S1, S5; cc-2.1.292.md Review spikes, S-skip). sub-human answers without next() only where its task gate blocks (classic.TaskCompleted), where its classic.UserPromptSubmit hook failed and refuses an @room it could not check (its .catch; the hook itself calls next(e) on every path and merges its answer), and for the /sub-human expansion whose join its command.run hook already ran (classic.UserPromptExpansion: the join hook beneath must not run twice). Its classic.PreToolUse hooks (mod/rows.ts, mod/consent.ts) call next(e) on every path and put their answer above it (mod/core/shim.ts mergePre).

entries.note: An answer {} (no text, no context) of a typed prompt adds no row at all: the command line is not echoed and nothing reaches the model; a {text} answer is the command's output row, shown under "sub-human: " (the hooking plugins' names) and read by the model with its echoed command line (local_command rows go to the API), and the model repeats it on its next turn (seen live), so the module answers {} and shows replies with $.ui.log. The built-in /rename NAME renames the session (its title and the session registry's name, the SendMessage address). mod/deliver.ts runs it with $.command.run after a /sub-human leave, so the session stops answering to NAME.CODE at once rather than at the next prompt (item 12).

A UserPromptExpansion block is drawn as a warning "UserPromptExpansion operation blocked by hook:\n<reason>" (never read by the model), and the expansion stops at the first block, before that hook's systemMessage is read: a block shows its reason alone. The classic join hook (no module) still answers this way.

A UserPromptSubmit stop (continue:false, a function hook's preventContinuation) keeps the person's row and adds two: an isMeta user row the model reads and a system warning row the person sees, both "Operation stopped by hook: <stopReason>". Nothing else ends a typed non-slash prompt without a turn and without a frame: a prompt.submit drop draws "Prompt dropped by a hook: <reason>" (and loses the person's row), an answer without next "Prompt not submitted: …". An @room's receipt is such a stop; mod/prompt.ts rewrites its warning row (session-append-notice-rewrite) and words the isMeta copy as a receipt that asks the model nothing (a session.append text rewrite, which the typings allow for any row).
